SYNTHESIZED — no real OpenCode store was available on this machine.

This fixture mimics the native shape of the OpenCode v2 SQLite session
store `<data_dir>/opencode.db` as executed by the golden test with
`rusqlite` (no committed binaries), following the real drizzle schema at
upstream tag v2.0.29 (`packages/core/src/session/sql.ts`,
`packages/schema/src/session-message.ts`, repo `anomalyco/opencode`):
`session_v2` (sessions; `directory` is the workdir, `version` the app
version, `time_archived` set on archived rows), `session_message`
(ordered by `seq`; `data` omits `id`/`type`), `session_part` (keyed by
`(message_id, ordinal)`; `data` is one assistant content part), and
`project` (for the `worktree` fallback). Timestamps are epoch millis, as
upstream stores them.

The captured session holds a user message, one assistant message whose
parts cover text + reasoning + a completed `edit` tool call/result pair
(keyed by `call_id`) + the step token totals on the message, an unknown
`future-part` part (maps to `system`, never dropped), a completed
compaction, a `synthetic` message with `description` + `text`, a
`system` message with `description` + `text`, an `agent-switched`
message, an `idle` message (skipped, no event), and a second assistant
message with two completed `edit` pairs whose inputs use `path` and
`filePath` respectively (so `files_touched` holds three repo-relative
paths). Three sibling sessions exercise the filters: a child
(`parent_id` set), an archived row (`time_archived` set), and a session
whose `directory` is outside the worktree — each with one message so the
filter (not emptiness) excludes them. Session ids, version, token
counts, and prose are invented. It is not a captured production database.
